01.r: The Egyptians put men in charge of Israel.
01.n: Gesenius: to put, to set, to place. The subject is the Egyptians of the verse before; the BSB names them.

02.n: The Hebrew says 'over it', the people taken as one body; YLT keeps the singular. Our English says 'them', as most translations do; the same holds for 'afflict them' and 'they built'.

03.r: The officials in charge of the work.
03.n: Gesenius: leader, commander, and he cites 'rulers over cattle' for this word in charge of other men's work. BDB: chieftain, chief, official, captain.

04.r: The gangs of Israelites put to compulsory work.
04.n: BDB: body of forced labourers, labour-band or gang, and names the slave-gangs of Israel in Egypt; the brief's lexicon gives 'slave gang' for this verse. Gesenius gives 'tribute', and YLT follows that sense with 'princes of tribute'; our register keeps 'forced labour' here, as the lexicons place it. The word is plural: the gangs.

05.r: States the purpose of setting the chiefs over them.
05.n: Gesenius: purpose, intent, becoming a particle 'in order that'. Most translations fold it into 'to'.

06.r: The aim was to crush Israel by hard work.
06.n: BDB: be bowed down, afflicted; this is the intensive form, to afflict or humble someone. Again 'it' in the Hebrew, the people as one body.

07.r: The heavy carrying work laid on Israel.
07.n: Gesenius: burden-bearing, wearisome and laborious toils, citing this verse; it is a plural noun. It is a feminine noun closely related to the one our register renders 'burden-labour', so it is rendered the same way. 'Their' is plural and most likely means the chiefs' burdens, those they imposed; that is a reading, the Hebrew does not say.

08.r: Israel built the cities under this forced work.
08.n: Singular in the Hebrew, 'and it built', with Israel as the subject; YLT keeps it.

09.r: The towns Israel was made to build.

10.r: Cities built to hold the king's stores.
10.n: Gesenius: storehouses, granaries, citing this verse. The KJV says 'treasure cities' and the DRC 'cities of tabernacles'.

11.r: The cities belonged to the king of Egypt.
11.n: Gesenius: Pharaoh, a common title of the ancient kings of Egypt. The brief's lexicon gives its meaning as 'great house'.

12.r: Marks Pithom as the object of 'built'.
12.n: This small word marks a definite direct object and has no English equivalent; it is counted here with 'Pithom'.

13.r: One of the two store cities.
13.n: Gesenius: a city of Lower Egypt, on the eastern bank of the Nile.

14.r: Joins the second city, with its own object marker.
14.n: The 'and' is joined to a second object marker, which has no English equivalent.

15.n: Gesenius: an Egyptian city, probably the chief city of the land of Goshen, built or fortified by the labour of the Israelites; the name agrees with that of several kings of Egypt.

_extra.23: καὶ (and): begins a third city added in the Greek.
_extra.24: Ὤν (On): the Greek adds a third city, On; the Hebrew names only two.
_extra.25: ἥ (which): part of the added phrase 'which is the city of the Sun'.
_extra.26: ἐστιν (is): part of the added phrase.
_extra.27: Ἡλίου (of the Sun): part of the added phrase, naming On as Heliopolis.
_extra.28: πόλις (city): part of the added phrase.

01.n: ἐπέστησεν, 'he set over', singular in the Greek.

03.n: ἐπιστάτης, overseer, one set over others.

04.n: τῶν ἔργων, 'of the works': the Greek reads the gangs as the work itself.

06.n: κακόω, to treat badly, to harm.

07.n: ἐν τοῖς ἔργοις, 'with the works', where the Hebrew has 'with their burden-labours'.

10.n: ὀχυρός, strong, fortified: the Greek calls them 'strong cities', not store cities.
